history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Buddhist monastery (Gelugpa/Yellow Hat school); keep-or-drop decision needed. Bomdila Monastery, properly Gentse Gaden Rabgyel Ling (GRL), was founded in 1965 by the 12th reincarnate of Tsona Gontse Rinpoche (born in Morshing, West Kameng; died 1966) as a replica of the Tsona Gontse monastery of southern Tibet; the 13th reincarnation later enlarged it with a large prayer hall, which was blessed by the 14th Dalai Lama in 1997. The complex comprises a prayer hall, a Buddha temple, and monks' quarters; senior lamas teach young monks Buddhist philosophy and tantrayana practices. Note the overlap with CSV row 67 (Lower Gompa): travel guides and the West Kameng district site describe Lower Gompa as the market-side division of this same GRL monastery — rows 66 and 67 are not fully independent entries.

name: Bomdila Monastery
town_description: Bomdila is the headquarters of West Kameng district, a hill town at about 2,500-3,000 m in the eastern Himalayas on the Tezpur-Tawang road. It is the gateway to Tawang and is noted for its gompas, apple orchards, and Himalayan views.

travel.road: Daily buses/taxis from Tezpur, Guwahati and Itanagar
